newsitem.title: USA: U.S Gulf gasoline differentials firm on Citgo fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S Gulf gasoline differentials firm on Citgo fire.

text.p: Gasoline differentials in the dense U.S. Gulf Coast refining region began firming straight away Tuesday morning on news Citgo's alkylation unit at its Corpus Christi, Texas, refinery went up in flames overnight.
"If their 'alky' unit is down, gasoline is definitely going to get stronger. It seems like there's a lot of talk this morning but nothing's getting done yet," said one trader.

Other traders noted that higher grade gasolines like premium or cleaner-burning reformulated blends were likely to strengthen since an alkylation unit cranks out high quality gasoline blending components ideal for such fuels.
Furthermore, traders said Citgo is said to be a net buyer of one such fuel -- the V-grade 93-octane premium conventional -- to feed its sizable retail operations.
But many traders said they had not yet heard Citgo making buying inquiries in the market for any grade.

Indeed, offers on the normally thinly traded "V1" summer grade premium fuel popped up 0.25 cent in the early going Tuesday to 4.50 cents over "M1" U.S. Gulf Coast regular unleaded on supplies for prompt delivery.
The M1 itself popped up 0.25 cent, with offers heard at 3.35 under NYMEX gasoline futures for June delivery.
No deals could be confirmed in early trade.

Prices on prompt summer-quality "A1" reformulated gasoline remained notional, but traders said they would almost surely firm above current levels of 2.00 to 2.50 cents over prompt M1, or between 1.25 cents and 1.00 cent under June futures.

The alkylation unit, which is rated at a capacity of 21,000 barrels per day (bpd), exploded in flames at 2222 CST/2322 EDT/0322 GMT/ Monday evening, according to emergency officials, who noted they will let the blaze continue to burn -- a process that may take between 24 and 48 hours.
The explosion and fire, the cause of which remains unknown, has also downed other unspeificied units.
The refinery can process about 132,500 bpd of crude oil, has 77,000 bpd of gasoline-producing catalytic cracking and 52,000 bpd of premium-gasoline producing catalytic reforming output.
"I'm sure the fire will lift prices. This market has been looking for something to move it," another trader said.
